hooks.text: Earth would keep orbiting if the Sun became a black hole.
Black holes do not act as cosmic vacuum cleaners from afar.
From far away, a black hole matches any body of equal mass.

title: What If the Sun Became a Black Hole?
description: Discover what would actually happen to Earth if the Sun turned into a black hole of the exact same mass.

beats.text: Earth would keep orbiting if the Sun became a black hole.
beats.visual: NASA illustration of the Sun and Earth in orbit
queries: Earth orbit around Sun illustration NASA

beats.text: Most people assume a stellar collapse creates an instant cosmic vacuum cleaner.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of a star-forming region or supernova remnant

beats.text: A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of a black hole with an accretion disk

beats.text: The boundary of no escape around a black hole is called the event horizon.
beats.visual: Event Horizon Telescope image of M87* black hole shadow
queries: M87 black hole Event Horizon Telescope

beats.text: Yet from far away, the external gravitational field of a black hole is identical to that of any other body of the same mass.
beats.visual: Diagram of spacetime curvature and gravity wells

beats.text: Our solar system would get much colder because the black hole emits no visible sunlight, but the planets would stay in their orbits.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a binary star system containing a black hole
queries: Cygnus X-1 binary system artist concept
